title: A bill to require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to extend the time period during which licensees are required to commence construction of certain hydropower projects.

claims.claim: Gives FERC authority to grant hydropower project licensees up to 6 additional years to begin construction, beyond the existing 8-year extension under the Federal Power Act.
claims.sourceSpan: additional 6 years beyond the 8 years authorized by that section
claims.note: Source: FERC may extend "for not more than an additional 6 years beyond the 8 years authorized by that section" (sec. 13 FPA). Calling the 8 years an "extension" tracks (c)(2)/(c)(3), which frame the sec.-13 period as an "extension" FERC "is authorized to extend."

claims.claim: Applies to projects that received their license before March 13, 2020.
claims.note: Covered project = a hydropower project FERC "issued a license before March 13, 2020" (date spans lines 23-24).

claims.claim: FERC may also retroactively reinstate licenses that expired after December 31, 2023 and before enactment.
claims.note: Window: construction period "expires after December 31, 2023, and before the date of enactment"; (d)(1) reinstates "effective as of the date of expiration" = retroactive. Subsection heading is "Reinstatement of Expired License."

claims.claim: Extends available FERC hydropower construction deadlines by up to 6 additional years.
claims.sourceSpan: additional 6 years beyond the 8 years authorized by that section

claims.claim: For projects licensed before March 13, 2020.
Allows reinstatement of licenses that expired after December 31, 2023.
claims.note: Brief compresses the window (omits "before enactment"), stated portion is correct; full window given in summary/top_lines/sections.

claims.note: Both are preconditions on the discretionary extension: FERC may extend "after reasonable notice and for good cause shown."

License Reinstatement.

claims.claim: Section 1 — Extension of Time to Commence Construction of Certain Hydropower Projects.
claims.sourceSpan: EXTENSION OF TIME TO COMMENCE CONSTRUCTION OF CERTAIN

claims.claim: FERC may extend the construction commencement deadline for covered projects.
claims.note: Discretionary "may ... extend"; covered project = FERC-licensed hydropower project.

claims.claim: Covered projects are those licensed before March 13, 2020.
Extension is by up to 6 additional years.
claims.sourceSpan: additional 6 years beyond the 8 years authorized by that section

claims.claim: In no more than 3 consecutive 2-year increments.
claims.note: "increments" faithfully maps "periods."

claims.claim: Upon licensee request.
claims.sourceSpan: on the request of a licensee

claims.claim: And for good cause.
The extension supplements — not replaces — the existing 8-year authority.
claims.sourceSpan: additional 6 years beyond the 8 years authorized by that section
claims.note: Additive: "not more than an additional 6 years beyond the 8 years"; "Notwithstanding section 13" preserves, does not repeal, the underlying authority.

claims.claim: That authority is under Section 13 of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 806).
claims.note: Source: "section 13 of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 806)."

claims.claim: The 6-year period begins only after the current maximum extension is exhausted.
claims.sourceSpan: begin on the date on which the final extension of the
claims.note: Begins when the final sec.-13 extension "expires."

claims.sourceSpan: reasonable notice and for good cause shown

claims.claim: FERC may reinstate licenses for covered projects.
For projects whose construction deadlines expired after December 31, 2023 and before enactment.
claims.note: What expires is the sec.-13 time period to commence construction; full window includes "before the date of enactment of this Act."

claims.claim: Effective as of the expiration date.
Reinstatement is retroactive to the license expiration date.
claims.note: Source: "effective as of the date of expiration of the license."

claims.claim: The new 6-year extension authority under this bill attaches from that date.

claims.note: Subsection (d) "Reinstatement of Expired License."

And grant the new 6-year extension starting from the expiration date.
claims.sourceSpan: the extension authorized under subsection (b) shall take

claims.claim: A project whose license lapsed in early 2024 could receive full retroactive reinstatement plus up to 6 years of new construction time.
claims.note: Illustrative example grounded in the (d) window (after Dec 31 2023) and the (b) 6-year cap; not a factual claim about a specific project.

claims.claim: The bill’s title describes a forward-looking deadline extension.
claims.sourceSpan: licensees are required to commence construction of
claims.note: Title: "extend the time period during which licensees are required to commence construction."

claims.claim: Section 1(d) creates a retroactive reinstatement mechanism that restores federal authorization to projects that had already lost it before enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: before the date of enactment of this Act
claims.note: Reinstates a license whose construction period expired before enactment; "federal authorization" = the FERC license.

claims.claim: The bill requires "good cause shown" for an extension.
It does not define good cause or establish criteria, leaving the standard to FERC discretion.
claims.note: Supported by absence: source states "for good cause shown" but supplies no definition or criteria; extension is discretionary ("may").

claims.claim: The bill applies only to projects licensed before March 13, 2020.
It does not explain the significance of that date or address treatment of projects licensed on that date.
claims.note: Supported by absence: "before March 13, 2020" excludes the date itself; source offers no rationale for the date and no on-the-date carve-out.

claims.claim: The bill does not address whether environmental review requirements attached to the original license must be updated before construction may begin under the extended deadline.
claims.sourceSpan: reasonable notice and for good cause shown
claims.note: Supported by absence: no environmental-review language anywhere in the text; extension conditions are only reasonable notice + good cause.

claims.claim: FERC authority to grant up to 6 additional years of construction-deadline extensions for hydropower projects licensed before March 13, 2020, in no more than 3 consecutive 2-year periods.
claims.sourceSpan: additional 6 years beyond the 8 years authorized by that section
claims.note: 6 years (b), before-March-13-2020 (a), 3 consecutive 2-year periods (c)(1) all verbatim in source.

claims.claim: FERC authority to reinstate expired licenses for covered projects whose deadlines lapsed after December 31, 2023, effective retroactively as of the expiration date.
claims.note: Reinstatement (d)(1); retroactive "effective as of the date of expiration."

claims.claim: Maximum extension authority for covered-project construction deadlines rises from up to 8 years to up to 14 years total extension time.
claims.sourceSpan: additional 6 years beyond the 8 years authorized by that section
claims.note: Both operands verbatim (8 years + additional 6 years); 14 = 8+6 is permitted objective arithmetic on explicit source figures.
